patterns.what_worked: Reading the six bench audits and the five desk journals as LEADS and then re-verifying every finding from source was the right order: several findings the audits raised were already fixed by later lanes (the Extras' three HIGHs, the /tt lb forwarding, the dead locale keys), and one audit line the fix-main-hunter journal had explicitly left out of scope -- the CharacterFrame OnShow adapter -- turned out to be the single highest-value unguarded hook left in the main add-on. Every change was proved by reverting it to RED on an isolated copy under /tmp/opencode and restoring the tree to green afterwards; nine reverts, nine reds, quoted in the desk journal.
patterns.what_was_hard: The edit tool refused several multi-line oldStrings whose content it had itself just written, which cost time and forced a switch to script-driven edits for the larger blocks. The coordination with the fix-main-restore lane worked but needed discipline: the Extras side was done first, the main side waited for the desk's done signal, and every main file was re-read immediately before its edit.
patterns.skill_gap: I should have checked the shape of the edit tool's multi-line matching earlier instead of discovering it one failure at a time. A one-line-per-edit discipline, or a small python helper for structural moves, is the reliable path for this codebase.

summary: Final defensive hardening pass over TacoTip 0.8.4 and TacoTip Extras 1.2.3: every Blizzard-frame and hooksecurefunc callback the Extras registers is now bounded and counted; the Extras' Options page has no silent no-ops; the main add-on's '/tacotip save' and '/tacotip default' commands now say what they did; the options panel's protected calls no longer discard their results; a hand-edited TacoTipConfig now reports what it repaired; and the two pane OnShow hooks are bounded so a raise can no longer unwind through the client's own frame script. Nine revert-to-fail proofs; all five validation commands green.
hardened: EXTRAS TacoTip_Extras/Frames.lua:69-88, 1335, 1336, 1339, 1384, 1385, 1388, 1393, 1398, 1401, 1404, 1407 -- the eleven callbacks registered on Blizzard frames / hooksecurefunc post-hooks are wrapped; a raise is caught at the boundary, counted (hookCallbackErrors) and named (lastHookCallbackError). Risk removed: a raise in a HookScript handler or a hooksecurefunc post-hook unwound through the CLIENT's own frame script, so the rest of Blizzard's handler never ran and the character/inspect pane was left half drawn with nothing in the add-on's diagnostics.

EXTRAS TacoTip_Extras/Options.lua:63-137, 1675, 1693, 1713, 1754 -- the counted action-failure boundary. 'Comfortable rows' and 'Shaman Blue' discarded the result of RankBrowser.RebuildUI; 'Open Server Leaderboard', 'Scan now', 'Reset enhancer settings', 'Restore TacoTip settings' and 'Reset summary positions' could do nothing at all. Risk removed: a ticked box with an unchanged window and no message and no count.

EXTRAS TacoTip_Extras/Core.lua:1128-1137 -- the /ttgsdebug surfaces block prints frame-hook-errors / last-frame-hook-error and options-action-failures / last-options-action-failure. Risk removed: a counter no user can see is a counter that cannot be acted on.

MAIN options.lua:700-715 -- '/tacotip save' with the mover closed was a total silent no-op; it now prints the same line the gearscore.lua bootstrap handler has always used and counts the refusal (TT.ev.moverSaveSkipped). A raising _Save is caught, counted (TT.ev.moverSaveFailed) and named. Risk removed: a documented command that did nothing and said nothing.

MAIN options.lua:673-699 -- '/tacotip default' printed its confirmation only when there was nothing to disable and stayed silent when a custom position really was cleared (inverted relative to the effect); it now confirms once after the reset, and the mover's _Disable call is bounded and counted (TT.ev.moverDisableFailed). Risk removed: the player never learned that their custom position had been cleared.

MAIN options.lua:1044-1094 -- openOptionsPanel no longer discards the results of Settings.OpenToCategory (twice) and InterfaceOptionsFrame_OpenToCategory; the failures are counted (TT.ev.optionsPanelOpenFailed / optionsPanelShowFailed), the last error is kept, and one plain chat line names the problem. Risk removed: a typed command that opened no panel, with no message and no count.

MAIN options.lua:316-470 -- the corrupt-saved-data ledger: the sanitiser already failed closed and recovered to the shipped defaults but did it in silence; the number of repaired settings is now counted (TT.ev.configRepairs), the first is named (TT.ev.lastConfigRepair) and /tacotip diag reports both. Risk removed: a player whose option had been silently reset had no way to learn it.

MAIN main.lua:3778-3791 and main.lua:4027-4038 -- the character pane's and the inspect pane's OnShow refreshes are now bounded and counted (TT.ev.characterPaneOnShowFailed / inspectPaneOnShowFailed, with the last error kept). Risk removed: a raise in either hook unwound through the CLIENT's own frame script, so the rest of Blizzard's handler never ran and the pane was left half drawn.
MAIN main.lua:4216-4232, 4466-4506 -- /tacotip diag prints all the new counters and names them in the PROBLEMS section.

not_hardened: The Extras' own OnEvent handlers (Core.lua:1382, Frames.lua:1463) sit on the add-on's own frames, so a raise aborts the add-on's handler, not a Blizzard one.

TacoTip_Extras/RankSync.lua handlePayload is not wrapped; the inbound parsing is already bounded and every refusal is counted, so the reachable raise is small, and wrapping the whole dispatch would blur the counters the release depends on.

gearscore.lua's TT_GS._itemRequestTime grows one entry per distinct item hovered and is never pruned; gearscore.lua is outside this pass's edit scope except for a guard around an existing call, and pruning is a behaviour change.
main.lua:369 pcall(cancel) discards its result; it is a timer-cleanup path with no user-visible artefact.

main.lua:3133 pcall(RequestLoadItemDataByID) discards its result; the shared throttle swallows the raw call's own error internally, so a counter at that level would almost never move. Counting the raw failure properly means a counter inside gearscore.lua.

The InspectFrame OnHide handler reads InspectGearScore / InspectAvgItemLvl without a nil check; they cannot be nil because the hook is registered inside TT:InitInspectFrame right after they are created, so a guard would be dead code.
The Extras' TacoTipExtrasDB corruption path and the sync wire were re-verified, not changed: both already fail closed, recover, and count every refusal.
